_comment: The ONE file you normally edit. The same file works on both machines - it picks the right section at runtime. Restart the client after changing it.

server._url_note: Your PC's Tailscale machine name. On the PC itself, localhost works. Point at http://localhost:7777/api/enforcement to test with mock-server.js.

safety._dryRun_note: TRUE = log what it WOULD block, change nothing. Leave true until the log looks right on BOTH machines.
safety._failClosed_note: Engine unreachable: true = keep the last known shield up. Matters more now - the Mac depends on the PC being awake.
safety._stale_note: After this long with no contact, notifications say STALE so you can tell a sleeping PC from real enforcement.
safety._neverBlock_note: Hard allowlist, never blocked even at shield_all. Keep one browser here so you can always reach the dashboard and spend a pass.

groups._comment: The server names a GROUP, never an app. You define what that means per machine. Domains are shared - a website is a website.

windows._firewall_note: Full .exe paths get a Windows Firewall outbound block. Gentler than killing - the launcher opens but cannot connect.

macos._note: macOS has no scriptable per-app outbound firewall, so no firewall list here. Process termination only.

shieldAll._comment: What shield_all means on both machines.

paths._notifyQueue_note: The SYSTEM task cannot draw to your desktop, so it leaves notifications here and the Ratchet-Notify agent shows them.
